1.w: A well-written song by Asaph. Why, O God, have you permanently rejected us? Why does your anger burn against the sheep of your pasture?

2.w: Remember your people whom you acquired in ancient times, whom you rescued so they could be your very own nation, as well as Mount Zion, where you dwell.

3.w: Hurry to the permanent ruins, and to all the damage the enemy has done to the temple.

4.w: Your enemies roar in the middle of your sanctuary; they set up their battle flags.

5.w: They invade like lumberjacks swinging their axes in a thick forest.

6.w: And now they are tearing down all its engravings with axes and crowbars.

7.w: They set your sanctuary on fire; they desecrate your dwelling place by knocking it to the ground.

8.w: They say to themselves, “We will oppress all of them.” They burn down all the places in the land where people worship God.

9.w: We do not see any signs of God’s presence; there are no longer any prophets, and we have no one to tell us how long this will last.

10.w: How long, O God, will the adversary hurl insults? Will the enemy blaspheme your name forever?

11.w: Why do you remain inactive? Intervene and destroy him.

12.w: But God has been my king from ancient times, performing acts of deliverance on the earth.

13.w: You destroyed the sea by your strength; you shattered the heads of the sea monster in the water.

14.w: You crushed the heads of Leviathan; you fed him to the people who live along the coast.

15.w: You broke open the spring and the stream; you dried up perpetually flowing rivers.

16.w: You established the cycle of day and night; you put the moon and sun in place.

17.w: You set up all the boundaries of the earth; you created the cycle of summer and winter.

18.w: Remember how the enemy hurls insults, O Lord, and how a foolish nation blasphemes your name.

19.w: Do not hand the life of your dove over to a wild animal. Do not continue to disregard the lives of your oppressed people.

20.w: Remember your covenant promises, for the dark regions of the earth are full of places where violence rules.

21.w: Do not let the afflicted be turned back in shame. Let the oppressed and poor praise your name.

22.w: Rise up, O God. Defend your honor. Remember how fools insult you all day long.

23.w: Do not disregard what your enemies say or the unceasing shouts of those who defy you.
